reader.requirement: At --std 85, a format 1 READ of an indexed file must select by the file position indicator against the current key of reference in the file's collating sequence (native, IX.2.3.4 GR3): no valid next record -> unsuccessful (46); optional file absent -> at end (GR10); after OPEN or START the first record with key >= FPI; after a READ the first record with key > FPI for a unique key, or the next duplicate in arrival order (then greater keys) for a key allowing duplicates; none found -> at end with FPI set to no next logical record; a record made available sets the FPI to its key of reference.

edition-consulted.switches: DialectBehavior.IndexedReadPreviousAfterOpenAtEnd (READ PREVIOUS directly after OPEN); only the PREVIOUS direction, which 85 refuses at compile time (COBOL0900), so the NEXT selection 85 reaches is the latest edition's code
DialectBehavior.IndexedDuplicateKeyStatusSequentialOnly: the 02 status of a random READ (status only; the FPI and key of reference it sets are the same at every edition)

reader.edition-search: grep 'Edition|DialectBehavior|CobolVersion' over IndexedConnector.cs, FileConnector.cs and KeyedIoEmitter.cs; the key collation is chosen by FileControlBinder.ResolveFileCollating (no COLLATING SEQUENCE clause -> native), which reads no edition and matches IX.2.3.4 GR3 at 85.
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no (for the record selected; READ PREVIOUS and the per-file COLLATING SEQUENCE clause do not exist at 85)
reader.witnesses-cover: part: pb810_read_46_takes_no_at_end covers rule a (46 after an at end) and the at-end path; not exercised by it are rules c (after OPEN/START), d (strictly greater after READ, including a record inserted after the FPI and a deleted successor), e (duplicates in arrival order, including a REWRITE that moves a record to the end of its duplicate set), and the native collating sequence under a PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE.

probes.printed: C-AFTER-OPEN 0010; C-START-NLT-0030 0030; D-AFTER-READ 0040; D-INSERTED-0045 0045; C-START-GT-0020 0030; D-AFTER-RANDOM-0030 0040; E-ALT-DUPS-ARRIVAL 0050 02, 0010 02; REWRITE 0020 AK->AAA 02; E-CONTINUE 0030 02, 0020 00, 0040, 0045, AT-END 10, ST 46; A-AFTER-AT-END 46; A-AFTER-FAILED-START 46; A-AFTER-FAILED-RANDOM 46; D-AFTER-DELETE-NEXT 0050
probes.expected: rule c >= FPI after OPEN/START; rule d > FPI after READ (FPI is a key value, so a newly inserted 0045 is found and a deleted successor is skipped); rule e duplicates in arrival order 0050, 0010, 0030 and the rewritten 0020 last (IX.4.6.4 GR15b); at end 10 then rule a 46 after at end, failed START and failed random READ (GR12)

probes.printed: PROGRAM-SEQ: LETTERS FIRST; 1001one 00; A001two 00; AT-END 10; START-INV 23
probes.expected: IX.2.3.4 GR3: an indexed file uses the native collating sequence even under PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE, so 1001 precedes A001 and no key is >= B000

probes.printed: error COBOL0900: READ PREVIOUS requires COBOL-2002 (targeting COBOL-85)
probes.expected: PREVIOUS is a later edition's phrase that 85 refuses

reader.notes: The connector holds the FPI as a key value plus the duplicate-set ordinal and the previous positioner (O/S/R), and SelectSequentialRecord picks >= after OPEN/START and strictly-after (key, ordinal) after READ, which gives rules c, d and e. Every probed selection matched the 1985 text.
